title: Rotation in [C II]-emitting gas in two galaxies at a redshift of 6.8
question: Can [C II] 158um confirm spectroscopically near-IR selected normal star-forming galaxies at z~7, and what are their [C II] luminosities, dust content and velocity structure?

data.sensitivity: 0.32 mJy/beam at 243 GHz in 50 km/s channel

what.value: HST and Spitzer photometry, photometric redshifts and [OIII]+Hbeta equivalent widths of the targets

evidence.quote: the photometry of these objects that was used in the selection of these galaxies in previous work(cite: Smit2015)

recipe.method: Pipeline calibration in CASA, CLEAN with natural weighting

recipe.goal: Detect [C II] and measure redshift and width
recipe.method: Extract spectrum, line-averaged map, Gaussian fit; S/N from 9000 random aperture measurements; blind line search with delta chi2>25

recipe.goal: Dust continuum limit and IR luminosity
recipe.method: Average line-free data, 3 sigma limit, grey body with beta_IR=1-2 and T_dust=20-60 K
Kennicutt scaling relations for SFR; MAGPHYS+HIGHZ SED fit excluding 3.6um
Per-pixel Gaussian fits (>5 sigma) for velocity gradient; estimates via Forster Schreiber approximation and thin exponential disk model fit with least squares and MCMC uncertainties
assumptions: symmetric rotating circularly symmetric thin disk with exponential mass density

evidence.quote: We derive a 3$\sigma$ upper limit on the IR luminosity of 1.3 and 1.1$\times10^{11}\,L_\odot$

not_stated_but_needed: Cell size, image size, and spectral cube channelization
Which channels were used for continuum averaging
Exact aperture/mask definitions for 1D spectra and half-max extraction
MCMC sampler, priors and chain settings of disk model
Conversion from continuum limit to L_IR (rest frequency, CMB correction)
missing_for_reproduction: Imaging cell/image size and cube channelization
score_reason: Public small dataset and key methods stated, but imaging parameters and model code missing.
rediscovery_reason: Public data, simple recipe, numeric line detections and redshifts.
